To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) Mobile computation offloading is not feasible for most of the apps in the Android market, (ii) Mobile software/data backups are not feasible for all the data stored in a smartphone.

(1) mobile software/data backup is feasible in the real world; (2) the energy consumption of mobile computation offloading is comparable to that of mobile software/data backup; (3) the bandwidth cost of mobile computation offload is higher than that of mobile software backup; (4) the cost of mobile computation is not always higher than that of software backup.

mobile computation offloading can be a feasible solution for the mobile cloud computing, provided that the off-clone is used only for a limited number of times and that the computation offloaded is not very demanding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How much does it cost to have an off-clone or a back-clone on the cloud?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the bandwidth costs of mobile cloud backup are not a big concern, but that the energy costs of mobile software backup are.
, while the offloading of computation is not feasible, mobile data backup is a viable option, but only if we are willing to accept some energy consumption on the device.
the use of mobile computation offloading is not feasible for most real-life scenarios, while the use of mobile data backup is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while mobile computation offloading is not yet a realistic solution, the mobile backup of software is a promising alternative.
mobile computation offloading is feasible in terms of bandwidth consumption but it has a high energy overhead.
, while offloading can be a feasible solution in some cases, the costs of backup are still too high to be considered as a feasible solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the bandwidth cost of off-clones is acceptable for most of the applications, the energy cost of back-clones is not.

mobile cloud computation offloading and backup systems do not come for free: They are bandwidth and energy intensive and their costs are not negligible, especially for smartphones with limited resources.
the bandwidth and energy costs associated to mobile computation offloading are not negligible, and they may not be affordable in real-life scenarios.
